title: B2B SEO: What It Is and How to Build a Strategy
excerpt: What B2B SEO is, how it differs from consumer SEO and how to build a B2B SEO strategy in eight steps, with keywords, content, links, AI search and a 90-day plan.

meta.rl_answer: B2B SEO is search engine optimization for companies that sell to other companies. It aims at qualified enquiries from buyers who research for weeks or months. Build it in eight steps: define your buyers, set goals, audit, research keywords by buyer stage, build the right pages, show expertise and trust, fix technical basics and earn links.
meta.rl_takeaways:
B2B buyers research for weeks or months and several people decide, so judge SEO on qualified enquiries and pipeline, not only traffic.
Small searches can be worth a lot. A term searched 30 times a month by the right buyers can beat one searched 3,000 times by the wrong ones.
Map keywords to buyer stages and build matching pages: guides, solution pages, comparisons, pricing and case studies.
Show experience and trust with named authors, sources, dates and proof.
Google says changes can take hours to months, and B2B sales cycles add more delay, so plan for six to twelve months.
Clear answers, consistent facts and independent mentions help in AI search as well as in normal search.
Tie search data to your CRM so you can trace deals back to their first search visit.
meta.rl_faqs:
What is B2B SEO? | B2B SEO is search engine optimization for companies that sell to other companies. It helps your pages rank in Google and appear in AI answers when business buyers search for a problem you solve, with the aim of qualified enquiries.
How is B2B SEO different from B2C SEO? | B2B has longer sales cycles, several decision makers, smaller and more specialized search volumes and a need for detailed proof such as case studies. B2C often has a shorter path and one buyer.
Is SEO effective for B2B? | Yes, when it is built around how business buyers research. Buyers read and compare before they talk to sales, so useful pages put you on the shortlist. It works poorly when it chases traffic instead of buyer questions.
How do I build a B2B SEO strategy? | Define your buyers and their questions, set goals tied to leads, audit your site, research keywords by buyer stage, build the right pages, show expertise and trust, fix technical basics and earn links, then measure and improve.
How long does B2B SEO take to work? | Google says some changes show in hours and others take months. B2B sales cycles are long, so a page may rank within months and the deal it influences may close later. Plan for six to twelve months.
What keywords should B2B companies target? | Target a mix by buyer stage: problem searches, solution searches, comparisons, pricing and proof searches. Include small, specific searches. They often have clearer intent and lower competition.
How much does B2B SEO cost? | There is no standard price. It depends on your site, your market, how much content you need and how much your team does. Get written quotes and compare the scope, not only the price.
Should I hire a B2B SEO agency? | It depends on your team. An agency brings strategy, writing, technical work and reporting at once. Many companies use both: the agency sets the plan and the in-house team supplies product knowledge. Ask for a written scope and how results tie to leads.
How do I measure B2B SEO? | Track organic traffic to key pages, rankings for a short list of searches, conversions such as demo requests, lead quality, pipeline and revenue influenced by search, and Search Console impressions and clicks. Connect analytics to your CRM.
How does AI search change B2B SEO? | Buyers ask AI tools for vendor ideas and explanations. These tools draw on clear, factual, well-sourced pages and independent mentions. Put short direct answers on your pages, keep facts consistent, be specific about who you serve and check what AI tools say about you.

meta.rl_g_glossary:
B2B | Business to business: a company that sells to other companies.
Pipeline | The set of sales opportunities that may turn into customers.
Topic cluster | A group of related pages that link to one another to show depth on a subject.
Search intent | The reason behind a search: to learn, to compare or to buy.
E-E-A-T | Experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust: qualities Google looks for in helpful content.
